Newspapers

Reported events, notices, advertisements and letters. OCR matches need visual checking; place names, vessels and matches to other surnames are excluded from Glasgow surname evidence.

275 distinct notices · 439 newspaper pages

Reviewed newspaper notices

275 distinct notices from 439 retained pages, earliest first. Reprints of the same notice are merged; 439 pages have saved inline excerpts. Open a notice for its clipping, reading and profile assessment.

How to read these notices

Cards lead with the person named in the notice; profile candidates are assessed separately. Birth cutoffs labelled “by c.” are estimates, usually assuming an adult professional was at least 18; open the birth note for the basis. Event groups are broad navigation aids built from each notice’s record type. A relationship filter identifies family wording in the notice, not a proved match to a WikiTree family.

Published 1737-11-03 · The Daily Gazetteer · p. 1

What the notice says

James Glasgow, styled Clerk, is appointed chaplain to the garrison of Edinburgh Castle by a royal commission reported read in the presbytery.

Evidence and identity limits

Full notice retained with Scotland section heading, Edinburgh dateline, preceding sentence, full appointment sentence and following paragraph start. Printed long-s glyph in Glasſgow is f-shaped and can produce OCR Glafgow; normalized surname reading Glasgow. 'Yesterday' refers to the Edinburgh Oct. 21 dateline; identity with the 1738 notice is not asserted. The 1737 and 1738 notices are a probable same-officeholder sequence, not a proved profile identity. Clerk is a clerical style, not evidence of a separate clerk occupation. Neither relative date is calculated from the newspaper issue date. Identity review (6 October 2026): 1737 Edinburgh report that James Glasgow, Clerk, was commissioned chaplain to the Edinburgh Castle garrison. Fasti and the Kilbirnie Fasti entry identify the Castle minister as James, son of Rev. John Glasgow of Kilbirnie and Margaret Scott: Glasgow-1140, strong.

Fasti Ecclesiae Scoticanae, new ed., vol. 1 (1915), Edinburgh Castle: 'JAMES GLASGOW, M.A. (Glasgow, 10th March 1718); commissioned by George II. 7th July 1737; ord. 14th Feb. 1738; died 9th Feb. 1746, aged about 48'. The notice's commission read in presbytery on 20 Oct 1737 ('yesterday' in the Edinburgh 21 Oct report) follows that 7 July 1737 commission. Fasti vol. 3 (1920), Kilbirnie, under JOHN GLASGOW, minister 1688-1721: 'He marr. (1) Jean ... Cunningham ... and had issue - Robert of Puddockholme, ancestor of the Montgreenan family: (2) Margaret Scott, and had issue - James, min. of Edinb

Who this may be

James Glasgow (Glasgow-1140)strong
[b. c. 1700-03-17; d. ?] · ordinand, minister of Edinburgh Castle
Why this candidate?

Fasti vol. 1: 'ord. 14th Feb. 1738'. The Edinburgh report dated Thursday 16 Feb 1738 (Old Style) says 'last Tuesday', and 14 Feb 1738 Julian was a Tuesday, so the date and office agree exactly. Fasti vol. 3 (Kilbirnie) names 'James, min. of Edinburgh Castle' as the son of Rev. John Glasgow and Margaret Scott, which is Glasgow-1140's baptism (Kilbirnie, 17 Mar 1700). The full argument and competitor eliminations are in group 1142270617.

Coverage, method & limits

703 pages catalogued · 556 original passages reviewed · 438 surname pages retained · 1 place-study page · 116 place/vessel/other-name pages excluded · 148 readings pending. Searches are selective and incomplete; these totals do not measure all newspaper holdings or all Glasgow mentions.

OCR hits and highlighted search words are leads. Saved excerpts may show only part of a notice; inspect the original page before treating a reading or namesake as proved. Missing issues, uneven digitisation, spelling variants and poor OCR can hide a relevant record. Free promotional access is temporary; original links may later require a subscription.

Search coverage and detailed qualifications

Irish pre-1800 priority search completed for the documented accessible result sets: broad surname queries, catalogue-led quoted names and abbreviations, and bounded spelling checks. Supplemental worldwide quoted-name and Glascow audits are recorded. Every confirmed pre-1800 page has an inline clipping. The 1800–1850 Irish extension remains in progress.

Coverage is a record of the named queries, provider collections, dates, loaded cards and actually screened positions. OCR omissions, name variants, unavailable titles and gaps in surviving holdings prevent a literal claim to every newspaper mention. A highlighted Glasgow can be a city, a vessel, a see, a military unit or another person’s address. Only inspected personal-surname passages are treated as surname evidence; clear preview dismissals are not full-page original exclusions. Original image, provider index/entity label and viewer OCR are different evidence. Viewer No matches can occur despite a printed name, as in the 1798 Secretary chest proclamation. Entity crime labels alone do not prove the name, a perpetrator or a conviction. Issue dates/pages normally follow provider metadata; checked printed masthead ranges and notice datelines are preserved separately. The 1793 Ordnance heading dates 25 and 27 September differ in parallel reports. No invented commission day or silently corrected year is supplied. Repeated advertisements and parallel archive scans are grouped by reading, with every issue/excerpt linked. They are not independent events or corroboration. Private-sale, adjournment and judicial-sale stages retain their distinct terms; offers do not establish completed transfers, bankruptcy or death. Approved inline PNGs are faithful bounded source pixels. Faded text and scan/fold damage remain visible and qualified; fuller parallel excerpts and originals remain linked. No full private viewer capture, reconstructed image or private browser state is published. Profile matches are confirmed, probable, possible or unlikely as individually assessed. Same name/locality, absent fields or a tree-only parent link do not identify a person. Uncertain before dates are upper bounds; estimated dates are not exact exclusions. An explicit documentary father–son statement does not identify either existing WikiTree profile. Postal addressees may be deceased; vessel William does not supply its master’s forename. Military selection or appointment reports do not prove completed service; allegations and proclamations retain their attribution. Core Irish pre-1800 displayed queries and promising original leads are closed. The 1800–1850 quoted-name pass records all 66 catalogue name forms in both Ireland and Northern Ireland (132 name/collection pairs), plus 15 bounded variant pairs. Current available result positions and promising surname passages have been reviewed; all verified retained surname pages have approved inline excerpts. Three provider limitations remain: John’s Ireland query is captured through the complete reported 108-image union of oldest/newest sorts without a physical End control; Ann’s Ireland query shows End after 13 cards against a 16-match header; Ellen’s current two-card run differs from a historic three-card run. A separately saved 1850 Margaret Glasgow marriage notice remains uncounted because Glasgow’s surname or given-name function is unresolved. These are bounded search and reading limits, not proof that every surviving newspaper mention has been found. OCR omissions, variants and unavailable titles remain outside a literal completeness claim; no live WikiTree relationship upgrade is claimed.
